budget_introduction.message: F-GC44: align end-to-end SWAP bridge with qualified F-GC30 numerical envelope
changes: temporal mode changed to Richards model certificate
accepted predecessor right derivative initialized to zero
budget_introduction.interpretation: The budget entered as part of a qualification-fixture numerical-envelope alignment.

fgc30_authority.finding: The admitted F-GC30 capability is a drainage-free predictor/tangent response. Its preserved limits explicitly exclude irrigation. The authority records do not establish an active-irrigation head-error requirement of 1e-5 cm.

fgc44_authority.finding: F-GC44 admits a deliberately narrow short near-equilibrium one-column/one-cell route and explicitly excludes irrigation and Ribasim.

active_irrigation_counterevidence.RM19: the unchanged inherited budget rejects all solver-successful active-irrigation retries
active_irrigation_counterevidence.RM20: forcing-switch correction reduces the certificate strongly but leaves a 0.23587665 cm bound
active_irrigation_counterevidence.RM23: independent same-horizon one-step versus two-half endpoint head difference is 0.04638380228385586 cm

conclusion: The repository supports HEAD_BUDGET=1e-5 cm as part of the admitted F-GC44 near-equilibrium qualification envelope.
The repository does not support transferring that numerical budget as a scientifically independent acceptance requirement for active irrigation.
Using the inherited budget to reject RM13B active irrigation is therefore fail-closed and conservative, but it is not a scientifically qualified application decision.
The 0.0464 cm RM23 refinement difference independently confirms a different temporal scale, but RM24 does not convert that observation into a replacement tolerance.
nonclaims: No replacement temporal threshold is proposed.
No existing F-GC44 canonical admission is revoked.
No claim is made that 0.0463838 cm is exact temporal error.
next_required_boundary: Define a prospective active-irrigation temporal acceptance contract independently of the RM13B pass/fail outcome. The contract should specify which hydrological outputs require temporal fidelity, how the error reference is constructed when fine-step refinement becomes nonlinear, and what quantitative application requirement justifies acceptance.
